Dear Counsel,

Thank you for sending Seller’s initial draft. Buyer has reviewed the draft and has the following principal comments.

1. Purchase Price. Buyer cannot agree to USD 45,000,000. Based on Buyer’s preliminary review and the risks that remain to be diligenced, Buyer proposes a purchase price of USD 36,000,000, subject to customary adjustments for cash, debt, transaction expenses, working capital, and any pre-closing leakage.

2. Closing. Please revise the closing mechanics so that closing occurs within 45 days after signing, subject to completion of confirmatory due diligence and satisfaction or waiver of customary closing conditions.

3. Representations. The current representation package is too limited. Please expand it to include customary seller and company representations, including title to the shares, authority, enforceability, capitalization, no undisclosed liabilities, compliance with law, tax, material contracts, litigation, employees/benefits, intellectual property, financial statements, absence of material adverse changes, and related-party matters.

4. Remedies. Please add customary indemnification provisions, including survival periods, caps/baskets to be discussed, special indemnities where appropriate, and an escrow or holdback to secure Seller’s obligations.

5. Confidentiality. Section 4 is acceptable in principle, provided it includes customary exceptions for disclosures to legal, tax, accounting, financing sources, regulators, and Buyer’s representatives and investors, in each case subject to appropriate confidentiality protections.

Please circulate a revised draft reflecting the above, or we would be happy to provide a mark-up.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 45,000,000 for the Shares, subject to customary adjustments for cash, indebtedness, transaction expenses, net working capital relative to a mutually agreed target, and any pre-closing leakage, in each case as finally determined in accordance with the closing statement procedures to be agreed by the parties.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur no later than 45 days after signing, subject to completion of confirmatory due diligence reasonably satisfactory to Buyer and the satisfaction or waiver of the conditions to closing set forth in this Agreement. At Closing, Seller shall deliver customary instruments of transfer for the Shares, resignations of directors and officers as reasonably requested by Buyer, payoff letters and releases for indebtedness to be discharged at Closing, and such other customary deliverables as are reasonably necessary to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby.

3. Representations. Seller represents and warrants to Buyer, subject to customary qualifications and disclosure schedules to be agreed, that: (a) Seller has good and valid title to the Shares, free and clear of liens other than transfer restrictions under applicable securities laws; (b) Seller has full authority to enter into and perform this Agreement, and this Agreement constitutes Seller’s valid and binding obligation, enforceable in accordance with its terms; (c) the Company is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing in its jurisdiction of organization; (d) the capitalization of the Company is as set forth on the applicable disclosure schedule, and the Shares constitute all of the issued and outstanding equity interests being sold; (e) the financial statements delivered to Buyer have been prepared in accordance with applicable accounting principles consistently applied and fairly present, in all material respects, the financial condition and results of operations of the Company for the periods presented; (f) except as disclosed, the Company has no material undisclosed liabilities; (g) the Company is in material compliance with applicable laws and permits; (h) the Company has timely filed material tax returns and paid material taxes due, subject to customary exceptions for taxes being contested in good faith; (i) the material contracts of the Company are valid and in force, and neither the Company nor, to Seller’s knowledge, any counterparty is in material default thereunder; (j) there is no material litigation pending or, to Seller’s knowledge, threatened against the Company; (k) the Company is in material compliance with applicable employment and benefits laws; (l) the Company owns or has the right to use the intellectual property material to the conduct of its business; (m) since the most recent balance sheet date, there has not been a material adverse change in the business of the Company; and (n) except as disclosed, there are no material related-party transactions involving the Company, Seller, or their respective affiliates.

4. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement and the transactions contemplated hereby are confidential and shall not be disclosed by either party without the prior written consent of the other party, except that either party may disclose such information to its legal, tax, accounting, financial, and other professional advisors, financing sources, regulators, representatives, affiliates, and investors or prospective investors, in each case to the extent reasonably necessary in connection with the transactions contemplated hereby and subject to customary confidentiality obligations or professional duties of confidentiality. Nothing herein shall restrict disclosures required by applicable law, regulation, legal process, or stock exchange rule, provided that the disclosing party, to the extent legally permissible, gives prompt notice and reasonably cooperates in limiting such disclosure.

5. Indemnification. From and after Closing, Seller shall indemnify Buyer for losses arising out of breaches of Seller’s representations, warranties, covenants, and agreements, subject to customary survival periods, baskets, caps, exclusions, mitigation obligations, and claims procedures to be agreed by the parties. Fundamental representations, tax matters, fraud, willful misconduct, and any agreed special indemnities shall be subject to separate limitations to be negotiated. The parties shall discuss in good faith whether any portion of the Purchase Price will be placed in escrow or otherwise held back to secure Seller’s post-closing obligations.

(3) Closing to remain subject to confirmatory due diligence satisfactory to Buyer in its reasonable discretion, no material adverse change, accuracy of representations, covenant compliance, third-party consents, payoff/release documentation, and delivery of all schedules and closing deliverables. (4) Representations to be expanded from the current high-level formulation into full customary private-company seller/company representations, with disclosure schedules delivered promptly and Buyer reserving comments after review. (5) Add/restored confidentiality covenant with exceptions for affiliates, representatives, financing sources, regulators, legal process, and required disclosures. (6) Indemnification to include: 18-month general survival; fundamental/tax survival through applicable limitation periods plus 60 days; deductible basket not to exceed 0.5% of purchase price; general cap of at least 15% of purchase price; fundamental reps/tax/fraud/willful misconduct outside the general cap; no cap for fraud; and special indemnities for identified due diligence matters. (7) Escrow/holdback of 10% of purchase price for at least 18 months to secure post-closing obligations. (8) Fix section numbering and conform cross-references.
receiver.message_back:
Dear Counsel,

Thank you for Seller’s revised draft. Buyer appreciates that Seller has incorporated several structural points, including adjustment architecture, expanded representations, closing deliverables, and an indemnification framework.

Price remains the principal open issue. Based on Buyer’s continuing diligence and the risk allocation still to be finalized, Buyer is prepared to proceed at a purchase price of USD 38,000,000, subject to customary cash, indebtedness, transaction expense, net working capital, and leakage adjustments. The working capital target should be set by reference to a mutually agreed trailing 12-month average calculated consistently with the delivered financial statements.

On the legal terms, Buyer requests the following revisions in the next draft:

1. Closing conditions should expressly include completion of confirmatory due diligence satisfactory to Buyer in its reasonable discretion, no material adverse change, accuracy of representations, covenant compliance, required consents, and delivery of payoff letters, lien releases, officer/director resignations as requested, schedules, and other customary deliverables.

2. Representations should be expanded into full customary private-company seller and company representations, subject to Buyer’s review of disclosure schedules once delivered.

3. The draft appears to skip from Section 3 to Section 5, and we do not see the confidentiality provision referenced in your cover note. Please restore/add a confidentiality covenant with customary exceptions for representatives, affiliates, financing sources, regulators, legal process, and disclosures required by law.

4. Indemnification should include an 18-month general survival period, fundamental and tax survival through the applicable statute of limitations plus 60 days, a deductible basket not exceeding 0.5% of the purchase price, a general cap of at least 15% of the purchase price, and separate treatment for fundamental representations, tax matters, fraud, willful misconduct, and any special indemnities. Fraud should not be capped.

5. Buyer requires an escrow or holdback equal to 10% of the purchase price for at least 18 months to secure Seller’s post-closing obligations.

Subject to the foregoing, Buyer remains willing to move promptly toward resolution of the remaining open points.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP
